titleEn: Pre-Renovation Home Inspection Checklist for Vancouver Homeowners (2026)
titleZh: 温哥华装修前检查清单 (2026)：业主必知
contentEn:
A thorough pre-renovation home inspection in Vancouver typically prevents $5,000–$25,000 in surprise costs once construction starts. This checklist covers what to check before signing a contractor agreement, what Metro Vancouver municipalities require, and how inspection findings change renovation scope and budget.

What Does a Pre-Renovation Inspection Cover?

A pre-renovation inspection is not a standard home inspection — it is a scope-defining assessment that evaluates what must be fixed, upgraded, or accommodated before, or during, your planned work. It covers four areas that generate the most change orders in Vancouver renovation projects.

1. Structural and Foundation

Vancouver's clay-heavy soil and documented areas of slope stability risk make foundation assessment essential for any project that opens walls or changes load paths. Key items:

  • Foundation type and condition (concrete slab, crawlspace, full basement)
  • Signs of settlement cracking, moisture ingress, or carbon monoxide intrusion from below
  • Floor levelness — differential settlement affects cabinet and tile installation tolerances
  • Crawlspace access and drainage — standing water in a crawlspace adds $2,000–$8,000 to a Reno Stars project scope

Most inspections run $300–$600 depending on property size and age. Asbestos testing adds $150–$500 on homes built before 1990.

2. Electrical Panel and Capacity

Major renovations — particularly heat pump installations, EV charger additions, or kitchen扩 — require adequate electrical capacity. An inspector checks:

  • Panel age and amperage — 60-amp, 100-amp, or 200-amp service
  • Circuit breaker condition and labeling
  • Aluminum wiring presence (common in Vancouver homes built 1965–1975)
  • Capacity headroom for planned new appliances

Most Vancouver homes built before 1985 have 60-amp or 100-amp panels. Upgrading to 200-amp is typically $3,000–$6,000 in Metro Vancouver and requires a licensed electrician and permit.

3. Plumbing Pressure and Drainage

Low water pressure or drain backups discovered after demo are disruptive and expensive. An inspector tests:

  • Static and dynamic water pressure — ideal range 45–65 psi
  • Water heater age and condition — units older than 12 years are renovation candidates
  • Main drain capacity and camera inspection of underground drains
  • Galvanized steel pipe condition — common in Vancouver homes built before 1980

Re-piping a Vancouver bungalow with PEX averages $4,000–$9,000. Discovering the need mid-renovation doubles the cost.

4. Building Envelope and Insulation

Vancouver receives approximately 1,500 mm of rainfall per year — the fourth-highest of any Canadian city. Building envelope failure is the leading cause of renovation-grade surprises. A pre-renovation envelope inspection covers:

  • Roof condition, age, and ventilation
  • Exterior wall cladding and windows — moisture penetration points, seal integrity
  • Attic insulation R-value and ventilation balance
  • Evidence of prior water damage or mold

For a typical Vancouver bungalow, upgrading attic insulation to R-50 costs $1,500–$3,500. Replacing windows during a renovation averages $800–$1,200 per window.

Permit and Strata Requirements in Metro Vancouver (2026)

Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, Surrey, Coquitlam, and North Vancouver all require permits for structural, electrical, and plumbing changes. Additional requirements:

  • Strata approval: Required for all condos and most townhouses in Metro Vancouver — adds 4–8 weeks to pre-construction timeline. Reno Stars manages strata application preparation as part of our standard project management.
  • Heritage designation: Vancouver Heritage Foundation guidelines apply to pre-1940 buildings — specialized inspections required
  • Asbestos audit: Required before demo for buildings built before 1990; disposal costs $500–$3,000 depending on scope

Real Project Examples from Reno Stars

Pre-renovation inspection findings regularly change scope. A Coal Harbour condo renovation revealed galvanized plumbing requiring full re-piping before kitchen and bathroom work could proceed. A Delta whole-house project uncovered insufficient electrical capacity, triggering a panel upgrade before a heat pump installation could be scoped. In both cases, the inspection finding was addressed before construction began — eliminating the change-order risk.

Frequently Asked Questions

When should I schedule pre-renovation inspections?

Complete all inspections 2–4 weeks before the planned construction start. This gives time to review reports, revise the scope, and adjust budgets before signing a contractor agreement. Discoveries made after demo starts are change orders — typically 30–60% more expensive than the same work negotiated upfront.

How much does a full pre-renovation inspection set cost in Vancouver?

A complete structural, electrical, plumbing, and envelope inspection for a single-family home typically runs $800–$1,800. Townhouses and older homes cost more. Asbestos testing adds $150–$500 for pre-1990 homes.

Does the city of Vancouver require a pre-renovation inspection?

Vancouver does not mandate a pre-renovation inspection as a condition of permit, but building officials may require specific structural or engineering inspections as permit conditions. For owner-initiated work, the inspection is risk management — finding issues before construction begins rather than during it.

Can I skip inspections to save money on a small renovation?

A cosmetic renovation (painting, flooring, fixture replacement) with no wall opening, electrical, or plumbing work carries lower risk. Any project that opens walls, adds circuits, modifies plumbing, or changes structural elements should have a pre-renovation inspection. The $500–$1,800 inspection cost is routinely recovered when it prevents a single $5,000 change order.
contentZh:
温哥华装修前的全面检查通常可以防止开工后出现 5,000–25,000 加元的意外费用。本清单涵盖签署承包商协议前应检查的项目、大温哥华地区市政的要求，以及检查结果如何改变装修范围和预算。

装修前检查包括哪些内容？

装修前检查与标准房屋检查不同——这是一份范围界定评估，评估在计划工程之前或期间需要修复、升级或配合的项目。它涵盖温哥华装修项目中产生最多变更单的四个领域。

1. 结构与地基

温哥华的黏土土壤和已记录的区域坡度稳定性风险，使任何打开墙壁或改变荷载路径的项目都必须进行地基评估。主要检查项目：

  • 地基类型及状况（混凝土板、爬行空间、全地下室）
  • 沉降裂缝、潮湿渗入或一氧化碳侵入迹象
  • 地板平整度——差异沉降影响橱柜和瓷砖安装公差
  • 爬行空间通道及排水——爬行空间积水会使 Reno Stars 项目范围增加 2,000–8,000 加元

大多数检查费用为 300–600 加元，取决于物业大小和房龄。1990 年前建成的房屋石棉检测另加 150–500 加元。

2. 电箱及容量

大型装修——尤其是热泵安装、电动车充电器增设或厨房扩建——需要足够的电力容量。检查员审核：

  • 电箱年限和安培数——60安、100安或200安服务
  • 断路器状况和标签
  • 铝线存在（1965–1975 年建成的温哥华房屋常见）
  • 计划新电器的容量余量

1985 年前建成的温哥华大多数房屋配备 60 安或 100 安电箱。升级至 200 安通常需 3,000–6,000 加元，需要持牌电工和许可证。

3. 管道水压与排水

开工后发现水压低或排水回流会造成中断且代价高昂。检查员测试：

  • 静态和动态水压——理想范围 45–65 psi
  • 热水器年限和状况——超过 12 年的设备是装修候选
  • 主排水管容量及地下排水管道摄像检查
  • 镀锌钢管状况——1980 年前建成的温哥华房屋常见

用 PEX 为温哥华平房重新布管平均 4,000–9,000 加元。在装修中途发现需求，成本翻倍。

4. 建筑围护结构和保温

温哥华每年降雨量约 1,500 毫米，在加拿大城市中排名第四。建筑围护结构故障是装修级意外发现的主要原因。装修前围护结构检查涵盖：

  • 屋顶状况、年限和通风
  • 外墙覆层和窗户——潮湿渗透点、密封完整性
  • 阁楼保温 R 值和通风平衡
  • 先前水损或霉菌迹象

为典型温哥华平房升级阁楼保温至 R-50 需 1,500–3,500 加元。装修期间更换窗户每个平均 800–1,200 加元。

大温哥华地区许可证和共管要求 (2026)

温哥华、本拿比、列治文、素里、高贵林和北温哥华均要求结构、电气和管道变更的许可证。其他要求：

  • 共管委员会批准：大温哥华所有柏文及大多数联排别墅需要——施工前准备时间增加 4–8 周。Reno Stars 将共管申请准备作为标准项目管理的一部分。
  • 遗产认定：温哥华遗产基金会指南适用于 1940 年前建筑——需要专项检查
  • 石棉审计：1990 年前建筑拆除前必须进行；处置费用 500–3,000 加元不等

Reno Stars 真实项目案例

装修前检查结果经常改变工程范围。Coal Harbour 柏文装修发现镀锌管道需要全面重新布管，才能进行厨房和浴室工程。Delta 全屋装修发现电力容量不足，在热泵安装范围确定前需要先进行电箱升级。在这两个案例中，检查发现在开工前得到处理——消除了变更单风险。

常见问题

我应该什么时候安排装修前检查？

在计划开工前 2–4 周完成所有检查。这有时间审查报告、修改范围并在签订承包商协议前调整预算。在开工后发现问题就是变更单——通常比提前协商的同一工作贵 30–60%。

温哥华的全面装修前检查套件费用是多少？

独立屋的结构、电气、管道和围护结构全面检查通常为 800–1,800 加元。联排别墅和旧房费用更高。1990 年前房屋石棉检测另加 150–500 加元。

温哥华市是否要求装修前检查？

温哥华不要求将装修前检查作为许可条件，但建筑官员可能要求将特定结构或工程检查作为许可条件。对于业主主动发起的工程，检查是风险管理——在施工开始前发现问题，而非期间。

小规模装修可以跳过检查以节省费用吗？

不打开墙壁、不增加电路、不修改管道或不改变结构元素的 Cosmetic 装修（油漆、地板、灯具更换）风险较低。任何打开墙壁、添加电路、修改管道或改变结构元素的工程都应进行装修前检查。500–1,800 加元的检查费用，通常通过防止一张 5,000 加元的变更单来收回。
